name: Sun
blurb: The star at the centre of the Solar System. It holds about 99.9% of the system’s mass.
stats: [["Diameter","1,391,400 km"],["Surface temperature","about 5,500 °C"],["Core temperature","about 15 million °C"],["Age","about 4.6 billion years"],["Spectral type","G2V"]]

name: Mercury
blurb: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. It has almost no atmosphere, so temperatures swing from scorching days to freezing nights.

name: Venus
blurb: Close to Earth in size, but wrapped in thick clouds and a dense carbon dioxide atmosphere that makes it the hottest planet.

name: Earth
blurb: The third planet from the Sun and the only place known to host life. About 71% of its surface is covered by water.

name: Mars
blurb: A cold desert planet with a thin atmosphere, huge volcanoes and deep canyons. Robots have explored its surface for decades.

name: Jupiter
blurb: The largest planet, made mostly of hydrogen and helium. Its Great Red Spot is a storm that has raged for centuries.

name: Saturn
blurb: A gas giant famous for its wide, bright rings made mostly of water ice. It is the least dense planet in the Solar System.

name: Uranus
blurb: An ice giant that spins on its side, tilted about 98 degrees. Methane in its atmosphere gives it a pale blue-green colour.

name: Neptune
blurb: The farthest planet from the Sun: dark, cold and windy, with some of the fastest winds in the Solar System.

name: Pluto
blurb: A small, icy dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt. It was called the ninth planet until 2006. A heart-shaped plain of nitrogen ice covers part of its surface.
